$note: Hand-authored overlay for the component contracts. The generator merges it onto everything
it can derive from the primitive itself (variants, tokens, states, parts, props), so only what
no source encodes belongs here: purpose, selection criteria, compositions, behaviour, and
anti-patterns. Keys must be section ids from src/app/sections.tsx and fields must be in
OVERLAY_KEYS (scripts/lib/contracts.mjs); gen-contracts fails on anything else.
Every claim here has to be true of the primitive or stated in design.md — this text is
published to consumers through the Claude Design specs.

note: alert-dialog has a primitive in src/components/ui and is named seven times in design.md as
the mandatory gate for every destructive action, but it has no section in sections.tsx and no
registry item — so it has no docs page, cannot be installed, and can carry no contract.
Its guidance is parked here rather than deleted. Move it up to a real key once the component
is documented and published. hover-card is in the same position (six mentions, not shipped).

rules: The only overlay without a close (X) — a destructive or confirming flow must force an explicit choice.
Every destructive action passes through one. Name what is affected and that it cannot be undone.

button.purpose: The one control for committing an action. Every clickable affordance is this primitive or composes it — a styled div or anchor loses the hover, focus ring, disabled and aria-invalid handling the variants already carry.
useWhen: The user commits something: submit, save, open an overlay, trigger an export.
A secondary or utility action sits in a table toolbar or page header — as an icon button (`size="icon-sm"`/`"icon-lg"`, usually `outline` or `ghost`) with an `aria-label` and a tooltip.
A destructive action has to stay quiet in a table row — `variant="ghost-destructive"`, neutral at rest and red only on hover.
dontUseWhen: The control only navigates. An anchor is the right element; `variant="link"` styles a button to read as text, it does not make it a link.
The user is choosing among options rather than acting — that is `select`, `tabs`, or `toggle`.
requires: An `aria-label` on every icon-only button, and a `tooltip` alongside it in page or table chrome.
A destructive action is gated behind an `alert-dialog` before it runs, and its outcome is surfaced with a `toast`.
Exactly one labelled primary action per view; the rest are secondary or icon buttons.
forbids: Hand-composing a quiet destructive button from `ghost` plus destructive utilities. `ghost` re-asserts `hover:text-foreground`, so the label goes neutral at the moment the tint turns red — use `ghost-destructive`.
Overriding the primitive's own classes to invent a look. Every appearance it can have is in `variants`.
A flat, stateless clickable element with no hover and no focus ring.
rules: A quiet destructive row action is `ghost-destructive`. Never hand-compose one from `ghost` plus destructive utilities — `ghost` re-asserts `hover:text-foreground`, so the label goes neutral exactly as the tint turns red.
Secondary/utility actions (export, refresh, filter) are icon buttons with an `aria-label` and a tooltip.

behavior.loading: Disable the button while its action is in flight. `disabled` and `data-disabled` both drop it to 50% opacity and remove pointer events, so a second submit cannot land.
behavior.destructive: A `destructive` button never runs its action directly — it confirms through an `alert-dialog` naming what is affected and that it cannot be undone.

a11yRequirements: An icon-only button carries an `aria-label`; the glyph is not an accessible name.
The focus ring is the `ring` token and stays visible — never `outline: none` with no replacement.
examples: `<Button>Save changes</Button>` — the single primary action on a screen.
`<Button variant="outline" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Export"><Download /></Button>` — a toolbar utility action.
`<Button variant="ghost-destructive" size="icon-sm" aria-label="Delete site"><Trash2 /></Button>` — a quiet row action.
antiPatterns: Reaching for `destructive` on a row delete, which paints a red chip on every row.
A labelled text button for every toolbar action, competing with the screen's one primary action.
Primary `default` on several buttons in one view.

input.purpose: The single-line text field. It renders the destructive border and ring from `aria-invalid`, so the invalid state is a data attribute rather than a class override.
useWhen: A single line of free text or a number is entered.
It sits inside a `field`, which supplies the label, description and error slots.
dontUseWhen: The value belongs to a known set — that is `select`, `combobox`, or `radio-group`.
The control needs an affix, icon, or button inside it — that is `input-group`.
requires: A programmatic label: `field`'s `FieldLabel`, or an `aria-label` where no visible label exists.
`aria-invalid` on the control when validation fails, paired with a `FieldError` that names what is wrong.
forbids: Re-styling the invalid state with border or ring utilities — the primitive renders it from `aria-invalid`.
A fixed px width. The field fills its container and the layout decides the measure.

behavior.error: Invalid means `aria-invalid` on the control plus an inline `FieldError` naming the problem — never a generic toast, and never a silently blocked submit button.

a11yRequirements: Colour is never the only error signal; the message carries the meaning.
antiPatterns: A required field that blocks submission with no inline message.
Hand-drawn focus styling that replaces the `ring` token.

select.purpose: Choose one value from a known set. The popup is portaled to the app root and matches the trigger width, so options line up under the value they replace.
useWhen: One value is chosen from a set too long for a `tabs` strip, or from one that grows.
A recurring job needs a control — a series selector, a date range — and then the same `select` appears wherever that job does.
dontUseWhen: The set is small and fixed and the choice switches panels — that is `tabs`.
The user needs to type or search — that is `combobox`.
The list holds actions rather than values — that is a `dropdown-menu`, which shrink-wraps instead of matching the trigger.
requires: A `SelectValue` in the trigger, so the current value is readable without opening the list.
Portalling left on, so no `overflow` ancestor can clip the popup.
forbids: A checkmark on the selected option in a single-select. The trigger value and the option highlight already say it; a check belongs only to multi-select.
Pinning a side that lets the popup run off-screen — the positioner flips and shifts by default.
Stretching or shrinking the list away from the trigger width.
rules: **No checkmark on the selected option** in a single-select — the trigger value plus the option highlight already say it. A check belongs only in multi-select.
The list matches the trigger width so options line up under the shown value.

behavior.error: `aria-invalid` on the trigger renders the destructive border and ring, exactly as on `input`.

a11yRequirements: The trigger is labelled — by a `field` label or an `aria-label`.
antiPatterns: Adding a tick to the chosen item because a design tool drew one.
A `select` for a job that a segmented control handles on another screen.

badge.purpose: A compact label for a status, a count, or a category. The variant carries the meaning, so the meaning survives a theme change.
useWhen: A row or card needs a status, a count, or a category label.
A commodity is being tagged — with that commodity's variant and nothing else.
dontUseWhen: The label is interactive. A badge is not a button, a filter chip, or a toggle.
The state belongs to a whole surface — that is the surface's own variant, e.g. an `alert`.
requires: A variant chosen by meaning: `outline` for neutral labels, a status variant only for genuine status.
forbids: Primary `default` for routine labels — it marks a single key highlight in a view.
A commodity variant on anything that is not that commodity.
Colour as the only signal; the text carries the meaning too.
rules: Neutral labels → `outline`; it is the default when unsure. Primary `default` is for a single key highlight only.
Commodity variants tag that commodity and nothing else.
a11yRequirements: The badge's text states the status; the colour reinforces it.
examples: `<Badge variant="outline">Draft</Badge>` — the right default when unsure.
antiPatterns: A row of primary badges, none of which is the key highlight.
A `success` badge used decoratively where nothing succeeded.

card.purpose: The standard content surface: the `card` token at radius `xl`, with header, content and footer slots sharing one 1.5rem content line.
useWhen: A coherent block — a metric tile, a chart, a table — is grouped on the page background.
A surface needs to sit one step above `background` in the elevation order.
dontUseWhen: The content is itself an overlay. `popover` and `elevated` sit above `card`, and a card inside an overlay flattens the stack.
The block is a page-level message — that is `banner` or `alert`.
requires: Content aligned to the card's 1.5rem content line. A table inside it aligns its first and last cells to that line, not to the 0.75rem cell padding.
forbids: A coloured strip along an edge to signal status — use the relevant component's own `-subtle` variant.
A hand-set radius. Cards are `xl` from the radius scale.

behavior.loading: The card keeps its frame and fills its content slots with `skeleton` blocks — never a raw loading gap or a bare spinner in place of the layout.
behavior.empty: No content is an `empty` state inside the content slot, carrying a retry action when the emptiness is a failed request.

a11yRequirements: `CardTitle` renders a `div`, not a heading. Where the card is a section in the page outline, supply the heading element and level yourself.
antiPatterns: A `border-l-4` status stripe down the card edge.
A card nested inside a dialog to re-create a surface the overlay already provides.

dialog.purpose: The centered modal for one short, focused action. It keeps a top-right close so a modal is always dismissible.
useWhen: A short create action of roughly one to four fields.
A focused, non-destructive confirmation.
dontUseWhen: The form is long or dense — that is a right-side `sheet`.
The action is destructive or irreversible — that is an `alert-dialog`, which omits the close on purpose.
requires: A `DialogTitle`; it is the modal's accessible name, visually hidden if the design shows none.
The default top-right close (X).
forbids: `showCloseButton={false}` — only `alert-dialog` omits the close.
Moving the close elsewhere, or hand-rolling a modal without one.
An inline scrim colour; the scrim is the `scrim` token.
rules: Short create actions (1–4 fields). Longer or dense edit forms go to a right `sheet` at 420px.
**Always keeps its top-right close (X).** Never `showCloseButton={false}` — only `alert-dialog` omits it.

behavior.destructive: A destructive confirmation is not this component — it is `alert-dialog`.

a11yRequirements: Focus moves into the dialog on open and returns to the trigger on close. Base UI does this; don't defeat it.
A surface opened from inside a dialog — a `select`, a `popover` — is a later portal sibling and paints above it without a new z-index.
antiPatterns: A twelve-field form in a dialog that should have been a sheet.
A non-destructive modal with the close removed.

sheet.purpose: The edge-anchored panel for longer edit flows. 420px on the inline edges by default, full width on mobile.
useWhen: An edit or update form runs to many fields.
A detail panel should keep the page context visible behind it.
dontUseWhen: The form is one to four fields — that is a `dialog`.
The flow is a destructive confirmation — that is an `alert-dialog`.
requires: A `SheetTitle`.
The default top-right close (X).
forbids: Widening past the default unless the content genuinely needs it — and then through the `--sheet-width` custom property the primitive reads, not a `w-*` override.
Removing the close.
rules: Default width 420px, full-width on mobile. Keeps its top-right close (X).
a11yRequirements: Focus moves into the panel on open and returns to the trigger on close.
antiPatterns: A sheet used as a permanent side panel — it is an overlay, mounted at the app root.
A `w-[600px]` on `SheetContent` instead of setting `--sheet-width`.

table.purpose: The data grid for text-first rows. It ships the row hover and the alignment that make every table in the product match.
useWhen: Data reads as rows and columns.
Density is high and secondary detail can move into a `tooltip` or `hover-card` rather than another column.
dontUseWhen: The rows are actions or navigation — that is a menu or the `sidebar`.
There is no data to show — that is `empty`, in the table's place.
requires: Wide tables scroll inside their own container rather than forcing horizontal page scroll; the primitive wraps for this.
The first and last cell in a row align to the card's 1.5rem content padding.
forbids: Icons in cells unless explicitly asked — cells are text-first.
A hand-rolled row hover. The primitive's light `primary` tint is what every table uses.
rules: The first and last cell in a row align to the card's content padding (1.5rem), not the 0.75rem cell padding.
No icons in cells unless asked. Rely on the primitive's built-in row hover.

behavior.loading: Rows render as `skeleton` blocks in place, keeping the column layout, rather than collapsing the table.
behavior.empty: No rows is an `empty` state with a retry action when a request failed.

a11yRequirements: A `TableCaption` or an `aria-label` names the table.
Header cells are `TableHead`, not body cells styled to look like headers.
antiPatterns: A metric and its delta crammed into one cell instead of moving the detail into a tooltip.
A first column sitting flush against the card border.

sidebar.purpose: The application navigation frame: a provider holding collapse state, a rail, and menus whose active item uses the component's own neutral highlight.
useWhen: Top-level navigation of the app shell.
Grouped, collapsible navigation that has to survive a route change.
dontUseWhen: The switch is between panels within one page — that is `tabs`.
The list is a set of actions on one element — that is a `dropdown-menu`.
requires: A `SidebarProvider` above any `Sidebar`; the collapse state lives there.
`SidebarMenuButton isActive` for the current item, so the active styling is the component's own.
A gap between menu items so an active item and a hovered neighbour never merge into one block.
forbids: Recolouring the active item with brand blue. The highlight is the neutral `sidebar-accent` surface, and the text and icon stay `foreground`.
Hand-rolling the highlight instead of composing `SidebarGroupLabel`, `SidebarMenuButton isActive`, and `SidebarMenuSub`.

behavior.loading: `SidebarMenuSkeleton` holds the menu's shape while its items load.

a11yRequirements: Items collapsed to icons keep an accessible name.
antiPatterns: A brand-blue active nav item.
Two parallel navigation patterns in one app shell.

toast.purpose: App-wide feedback for a completed interaction. One `Toaster` is mounted near the app root; everything else is the imperative `toast()` call from `sonner`.
useWhen: An interaction has no other visible result — a saved form, a toggled switch.
The outcome of a destructive action needs reporting after its confirmation.
dontUseWhen: The message belongs to one field — that is inline validation through `field`.
The message is a persistent page-level condition — that is `banner` or `alert`.
requires: A title on every toast; the description row collapses when empty.
A variant matching the outcome: `toast.success` for confirmation, `toast.warning` for a negative-but-expected result, `toast.error` for a genuine failure.
forbids: More than one `<Toaster>` in an application.
A neutral `toast()` for a success or an error.

behavior.error: A failed action surfaces a toast and keeps the user's input intact — the form is not cleared.

a11yRequirements: The toast text carries the meaning; the variant's colour only reinforces it.
examples: `import { toast } from "sonner"` — the `Toaster` is the only export of the registry item; the call comes from sonner itself.
`toast.error("Could not save site", { description: "The gateway did not respond." })`
antiPatterns: A save that completes silently.
A failure reported by colour alone, with no title.

rules: **Shrink-wraps to its widest item.** Never stretch it to the trigger width or pad items to a fixed width.
Portaled to the app root, so no `overflow` ancestor can clip it. It flips and shifts to stay in the viewport.

**Pick the variant by the surface underneath.** Plain `background`/`card` → `default`. A tinted surface or any overlay → `adaptive` or `line`; the `muted` track has no lightness step left there and the strip vanishes.
Never hand-tint a `TabsList` with a `bg-*` override to fix that — switch the variant.
Shrink-wraps to its content — never a `max-w` or fixed width that forces wrapping.
Portaled and viewport-aware; never pin a side that lets it run off-screen.
Validation is inline and specific, via `FieldError` + `aria-invalid`. A description and an error that swap in one position take the same type token, or the layout shifts.
Pair with a retry action on async failure — never a blank screen or an endless spinner.
Use for loading, with `spinner` and `empty` for the other two states. Never a raw loading gap.
